who.value: casual seller starting a new listing

job.value: start a new listing or pick up a draft

arrivedFrom.value: the Sell tab in the bottom bar

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: 'List anything yourself' and 'Create a listing' are clear, but five near-identical scanner tiles muddy what the screen is for.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: Six entry cards compete; 'Snap scanner B' has a teal outline while 'Create a listing' is the larger card, so there is no single obvious way in.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Snap scanner C — Toggle in camera', 'D — Toggle at top', 'E — Shelf + toggle' describe design variants, not what a seller gets.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'Snap scanner', 'Shelf + toggle' and the A–E letter badges are internal terms no seller knows.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: Starting a listing is a fair choice, but picking among five scanner variants is not a decision a seller can make.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: All five scanner variants are laid out up front instead of one entry point.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: The lettered variant tiles are review content for the design team, not for a seller starting a listing.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Tile labels are short; there is no paragraph to read.
